To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microwave field destroys the quantum coherence in superconducting junctions and that this effect results in strong suppression of the current and the differential conductance.
the microwave field leads to the effective cooling of the quasiparticle distribution and the suppression of the excess current in the superconducting weak link.
the ac field destroys the phase-coherent transport and leads to effective subgap cooling of quasiparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of charge transport in superconductor-ferromagnet-superconductor (SFS) junctions, which are of interest for both fundamental and applied physics.
the investigation of nonequilibrium effects in superconducting nanostructures and their impact on the charge transport in superconductor/normal-metal/superconductor (SNS) junctions.
the microscopic theory of charge transport in supercondcuting weak links.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the excess current and its temperature dependence are strongly affected by microwave radiation, while the conductance of a superconductor-insulator-superconductor weak link remains practically unchanged.
the microwave field suppresses the Andreev reflection processes, and hence the excess current, and that the conductance is reduced by the effective cooling of the subgap quasielectrons.

the excess current is suppressed due to nonequilibrium effects, and the conductance is suppressed due to a combination of nonequilibrium effects and the microwave induced suppression of phase coherence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how to use the microwave field to control the transport properties of superconductive weak links and that we have found new ways to study nonequilibrium phenomena in superconducting structures.
the nonequilibrium effects in superconducting nanostructures are of crucial importance for their charge transport properties and have to be taken into account when analyzing experimental results.
the microwave field can be used as a tool to control the charge transport in a superconducting weak link.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the excess current in the subgap region can be strongly reduced by a microwave field.
the excess current in a superconducting weak link can be strongly suppressed by a microwave field.
in the presence of microwave field the weak link behaves as a normal diffusive contact with a temperature of the order of 0.1 K.
